title: Quentin and the Group Chat
premise: Theo Kavanagh, a seventeen-year-old coder, runs an anonymous group chat that quietly exposes wrongdoing at Marrow Creek High — until a forced semester project pairs him with Quentin Vale, the golden-boy class president who has spent a year trying to unmask him. Digging into the town's centennial Founders' Pageant for their project, they uncover that the Vale family's inheritance — and the pageant itself — rests on a buried injustice done to Theo's own ancestors. As Quentin's family threatens to demolish the historic theater that hosts the final audition, the two rivals must expose the truth together, choosing justice outside the law over their legacies. The book ends with the pageant saved, the inheritance redirected to a community trust, and Theo finally posting under his own name.
about_author: J. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former debate coach who grew up in a small river town obsessed with its own founding myths. They write stories about teenagers who refuse to accept the histories they're handed.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Account
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He runs the group chat 'MarrowCreekLeaks' from his bedroom, exposing a stolen fundraiser, and nearly slips when a classmate quotes his own post back to him. Establishes his paranoia, his coding skill, and his rule: never get attached. Emotional beat: the lonely thrill of invisible power.

chapters.title: Nemesis, Assigned
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Civics teacher Ms. Okafor announces semester-long paired projects and reads the worst possible name: 'Kavanagh and Vale.' Quentin smirks; Theo's stomach drops. Emotional beat: dread disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: Golden Boy
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. We see his gilded life — the Vale name on the theater marquee, his mother's campaign for town council, his father's expectations — and the crack in it: he suspects the anonymous account is someone at school, and he intends to find them. Emotional beat: ambition curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Ground Rules
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. First project meeting in the library. Quentin proposes 'The Founders' Pageant: A Century of Marrow Creek Tradition.' Theo agrees only because the topic is boring enough to hide behind. They set hostile ground rules. Emotional beat: wary truce.

chapters.title: The Archive Basement
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Research at the historical society; Quentin knows every archivist by name. He catches Theo photographing a sealed box of 1920s ledgers and files it away. Emotional beat: curiosity he refuses to name.

chapters.title: MarrowCreekLeaks Strikes Again
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The account exposes the athletic department's budget fraud. Quentin publicly vows on the school broadcast to identify the leaker by winter break. Theo watches his nemesis become his hunter. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Late night with the 1923 ledger: the Kavanagh family's theater deed, transferred to 'E. Vale' the week after a fire no one mentions. Theo's hands shake. Emotional beat: the past reaching through the page.

chapters.title: Group Project
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Working session at Theo's cluttered apartment; Quentin meets Theo's grandmother, who goes silent at the mention of the old theater. Quentin notices what Theo wants him not to. Emotional beat: an unwelcome flicker of empathy.

chapters.title: The Pageant Auditions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They observe auditions for the centennial pageant at the Vale Theater. Theo's friend Priya auditions; the theater's magic gets under Theo's skin despite himself. Emotional beat: reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the archive, Quentin finds the 1923 fire report — suppressed, signed off by his great-great-grandfather. The Kavanaghs were blamed. Quentin sits with it for a long time. Emotional beat: the floor tilting.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both boys separately arrive at the same conclusion and say nothing, each testing the other with loaded questions about 'historical accuracy.' Emotional beat: two liars circling.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Grows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The anonymous account gains hundreds of followers; someone starts posting things Theo didn't write — cruel, personal. His tool is slipping out of his control. Emotional beat: power becoming peril.

chapters.title: Priya's Solo
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Priya, Theo's best friend, confronts Quentin about why he's really paired with Theo. Her bluntness lands; Quentin lies, and hates that he lies. Emotional beat: guilt with a face.

chapters.title: The Deed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's grandmother finally tells the family story: the fire, the stolen deed, the Kavanaghs run out of town. She makes Theo promise not to poke the Vale hornet's nest. Emotional beat: inherited grief.

chapters.title: Winter Break Stakeout
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both boys independently stake out the historical society during break, catch each other, and end up splitting fries at the diner, comparing notes for the first time. Emotional beat: the truce becoming real.

chapters.title: Quentin's Father
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin asks his father about the fire. The answer is smooth, rehearsed, and wrong — and his father announces the theater will be sold to developers after the pageant. Emotional beat: betrayal at the dinner table.

chapters.title: The Impostor
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The fake posts escalate: a cruel rumor about Priya. Theo must choose — expose the impostor and risk exposure himself, or let his account's credibility die. Emotional beat: a hacker's crisis of conscience.

chapters.title: An Uneasy Alliance
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Quentin figures out the account is Theo — and instead of exposing him, says 'I want to help.' Theo doesn't trust it, but he's out of options. Emotional beat: enemies shaking hands over a shared secret.

chapters.title: Tracing the Ghost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo and Quentin trace the impostor's posts to a school IP: it's Devon Marsh, Quentin's campaign manager, feeding Quentin's mother opposition research. Emotional beat: the conspiracy widens.

chapters.title: The Founders' File
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In his father's study, Quentin photographs the full Vale file: the forged fire report, the coerced deed, letters showing the Kavanaghs were paid to disappear. His inheritance, documented. Emotional beat: grief for a name.

chapters.title: What Inheritance Means
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo and his grandmother argue — she wants the past buried; he wants it printed. 'They'll destroy you,' she says. He hears: they destroyed us once already. Emotional beat: generational rupture.

chapters.title: Midterm Presentation
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Their project presentation whitewashes the pageant's history — Quentin delivers it flawlessly and feels sick. Ms. Okafor keeps them after: 'You two are lying about something. Find the real story.' Emotional beat: complicity.

chapters.title: Devon's Leverage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Devon discovers Theo is the account owner and blackmails him: stay quiet about the forged posts, or the whole school learns. Theo tells Quentin — the first time he's ever handed someone his vulnerability. Emotional beat: trust as a gamble.

chapters.title: The Counterfeit Pageant
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Rehearsals reveal his mother has rewritten the centennial script to glorify the Vales and erase the Kavanaghs entirely. Priya's solo is cut. The theater's fate and the town's memory are the same fight. Emotional beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Found Family, Formalized
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, Quentin, and Priya form their own group chat — real names this time — to plan. They call it 'the Pageant Truthers' as a joke, but it feels like something older: an alliance. Emotional beat: warmth after isolation.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They debate going public with the forged deed: lawyers, defamation, Quentin's family's ruin, Theo's family's old wounds. Justice outside the law means no protection. They decide to do it anyway. Emotional beat: resolve.

chapters.title: Devon Strikes
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Devon leaks doctored screenshots framing Theo's account for harassment. Theo is suspended pending investigation; his grandmother is humiliated at the council meeting. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Quentin's Choice
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. His father offers him everything — the theater board seat, the family legacy — if he disavows Theo publicly. Quentin stands in the empty theater and makes his decision. Emotional beat: the heir refusing the inheritance.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. With Theo suspended, Quentin and Priya work alone, and Quentin feels the weight of what Theo carried invisibly for years. He posts to MarrowCreekLeaks himself, under Theo's guidance by contraband phone call. Emotional beat: taking up another's burden.

chapters.title: The Fire Report, Published
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. From his suspension exile, Theo orchestrates the release of the 1923 documents through the account — now co-signed by 'Q.V.' The town erupts; the council meeting overflows. Emotional beat: the dam breaking.

chapters.title: Mother's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin's mother, mid-campaign, must answer for the family file. She knew. Quentin watches her choose the campaign over the truth on live TV, and something in him finishes breaking — and finishes freeing. Emotional beat: disillusionment as liberation.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. School board hearing on Theo's suspension. Priya testifies, Quentin testifies against his own mother's operation, and the doctored screenshots unravel under Devon's panicked cross-examination. Emotional beat: truth as a team sport.

chapters.title: Reinstated
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo walks back into school to actual applause, which he finds more terrifying than any exposure. Devon transfers; Ms. Okafor gives them an A-in-progress and a warning: 'The pageant is in three weeks.' Emotional beat: vindication, fragile.

chapters.title: The Developer's Deadline
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The sale of the theater closes the week after the pageant. The council, stung by scandal, might block it — if the pageant itself proves the theater's living worth. The final audition becomes the battleground. Emotional beat: a clock starting.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Pageant
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The trio pitches a restored script — the real centennial story, Kavanaghs included. The council hesitates; Theo's grandmother, watching, finally offers the family's archive to the production. Emotional beat: reconciliation offered.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Days before the audition, the restored script's master file is deleted and the theater's power is 'accidentally' cut. Theo rebuilds from backups while Quentin confronts the saboteur: his own father. Emotional beat: fury and heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The audition night: candlelit, packed, standing-room. Priya sings the restored solo; Quentin's father walks out; the council members stay in their seats, unmoving, until the last note. Theo, in the booth, runs the lights — visible at last. Emotional beat: triumph earned in public.

chapters.title: The Trust
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the aftermath, the Vales settle: facing exposure and Quentin's testimony, his father signs the theater and disputed inheritance into a community land trust. Quentin signs as a witness, not an heir. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Under His Own Name
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Final chapter. Theo posts a farewell to MarrowCreekLeaks — signed 'Theo Kavanagh' — and the group chat becomes an open town archive moderated by students. At the pageant's closing night, his grandmother takes a bow onstage. Emotional beat: visibility, chosen at last.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Group Chat
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later: the theater hosts a student-run history night; Theo and Quentin, now friends and co-editors of the archive, argue happily about their next investigation. The last message in the chat is Ms. Okafor's: 'Found your real story. A-plus.' Emotional beat: the tradition, saved and shared.
